guide.summary: Internal use, one Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none); Public app for many Zendesk customers (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal use, one Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for many Zendesk customers (app review).

composio.note: Composio lists Zendesk as managed OAuth, good for prototypes. For launch, use your own client ID and secret in a custom auth config.

need_own_app.answer: For prototypes, Composio's managed app works. For a launch with branding, dedicated quota or custom scopes you need your own OAuth client, and for many customers it must be a Zendesk-approved global client.
reasons: Managed app shows 'Composio wants to access your account' on the consent screen
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need
Multi-customer apps must use a global OAuth client approved by Zendesk

prerequisites.title: Zendesk admin access
prerequisites.detail: Creating an OAuth client needs a Zendesk account with admin access, or an agent with the Manage APIs permission via the API.

prerequisites.title: Sponsored developer account with d3v- prefix
prerequisites.detail: Global client requests are only accepted from accounts whose subdomain has the d3v- prefix. You can request a sponsored account from Zendesk.

prerequisites.title: Marketplace developer portal registration
prerequisites.detail: Register your organization at apps.zendesk.com and complete the organization profile, which Zendesk reviews.

steps.title: Create OAuth client in Admin Center
steps.detail: An admin creates the client under Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients, or via POST /api/v2/oauth/clients. Save the secret immediately, as it is shown only once.
steps.done_when: You hold the client identifier and secret.

steps.title: Choose scopes and prepare redirect URI
steps.detail: Draft the narrowest scope list from the endpoints the agent calls, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard. The redirect URI must match the client exactly.
steps.done_when: Scopes and redirect URI are registered on the client.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API using your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection works.

steps.title: Prepare production-ready client values
steps.detail: Use a client identifier prefixed zdg- that represents your product, complete every field even if optional, and note the secret and identifier before requesting.

steps.title: Prepare app ZIP, profile and compliance answers
steps.detail: Draft the profile text, check the ZIP against the branding guidelines, and prepare compliance answers and the privacy policy URL.
steps.done_when: The ZIP passes automatic checks without errors.

steps.title: Submit profile, app and terms
steps.detail: Submit the profile and app in the Marketplace developer portal, answer all mandatory compliance questions and accept the Terms & Conditions.
steps.done_when: Submission is accepted by the portal.

steps.title: Request global OAuth client
steps.detail: In the portal select Global OAuth, click Request new OAuth, and complete the form with your subdomain and scopes. Do this when the app is finished.
steps.done_when: You receive an email and ticket reference.

steps.title: Wait for Zendesk approval
steps.detail: Zendesk reviews the app and the global client request. If rejected, resubmit a corrected ZIP with Submit Update.
steps.done_when: Approval is received and the local client is converted to global.

traps.title: Losing access after global conversion
traps.detail: Access to the client administration page is lost once the local client becomes global. Note the secret and identifier before requesting.

traps.title: Customers' own credentials are not allowed
traps.detail: Third-party apps must not use a customer's API tokens or their own OAuth client, listed or not. Multi-customer apps must use a global client.

traps.title: Review times may exceed the stated 1-3 weeks
traps.detail: A developer reported almost three weeks under validation, and Zendesk confirmed a surge pushed responses past normal SLAs.

traps.title: Scopes outside the allowed list fail
traps.detail: A request for a scope outside the client's allowed scopes fails with 400 invalid_scope. If no scope is specified, the token gets full read and write access.

traps.title: Authorization is per subdomain
traps.detail: Each customer authorizes for their own Zendesk subdomain, and the authorization URL uses that subdomain.

traps.title: Zendesk Sell and Sunshine bots differ
traps.detail: The global client process applies only to Zendesk Support and Chat. Sell needs a Multi-User Application, and Sunshine Conversations bots need a separate token.

traps.title: Short-lived tokens
traps.detail: Access tokens expire automatically. Clients created on or after April 30, 2026 default to 30-minute access tokens and 30-day refresh tokens.

blockers.what_it_means: The request came from an account without the d3v- prefix, or the values do not match the local client.
blockers.what_to_do: Use a sponsored d3v- account and recreate the matching values on its local client.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check that identifier, prefix and fields match before submitting.

blockers.what_it_means: Zendesk found problems with the app or listing.
blockers.what_to_do: Fix the issues and resubmit a corrected ZIP with Submit Update.
blockers.agent_can_help: Review the ZIP for errors and branding compliance before resubmitting.

blockers.what_it_means: The requested scope is outside the client's allowed scopes.
blockers.what_to_do: Request only allowed scopes, or have the allowed list updated.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare requested scopes with the client's allowed list.

open_questions: Is there a documented turnaround for global OAuth client requests alone? Ask Zendesk through the ticket reference from the request, or check the Marketplace portal.
Which scopes need extra review? The docs do not say; check the OAuth scopes page or ask Zendesk.
Does a preview app with a global client skip the full public review? Confirm with Zendesk support.
